My 15-year-old terrier Jake has battled allergies his whole life, but last year things got really bad — he developed a demodectic infection that led to secondary skin infections, leaving his skin black and scaly. He was miserable. Previous vets had him on daily medicated baths that were only making things worse.

From the very first visit, Dr. Richman was different. He didn't just treat the symptoms — he went looking for the root cause. Through a thorough round of testing, he diagnosed Jake with Cushing's disease, treated it, and then continued to uncover and address other health issues beyond his specialty, coaching me through a thoughtful, systematic approach to help Jakey.

Dr. Richman is brilliant, investigative, professional, and genuinely caring. Jake — a dog who has always hated the vet — is actually happy when we walk through their door. His skin is almost completely back to normal, and he's eating and barking again.

I am so grateful for Dr. Richman and the entire team at Vet Skin and Ear. Thank you!

I booked an appointment six months in advance and heard absolutely nothing from this clinic in the interim — no confirmation email, no text, no call, no reminder of any kind. Then I get hit with a $105 no-show fee for an appointment I had no realistic way to remember without a single touchpoint over half a year.

I'll let other readers decide which it is. I won't be back, and I'd encourage anyone considering this clinic to ask up front exactly what their reminder policy is and get the answer in writing.

Five Stars Is Not Enough for Dr. Richman and His Team

I rarely write reviews, but this one feels important. Our 10-year-old dog, Frank, has suffered from chronic, severe ear and skin infections for over seven years. In the past, multiple veterinarians and even a previous dermatologist told us his only option was radical surgery: removing both ear canals and eardrums and sewing the ears closed—an irreversible procedure that would have left him completely deaf. We could never bring ourselves to do that.

Five years ago, we tried a different procedure elsewhere, hoping for improvement. Not only did it fail, but during the process Frank had a terrifying panic attack in their crate, went into heat stroke, and nearly died. For years afterward, his ears never improved, and this past year he had been going downhill so quickly that we thought we were approaching the end of his life.

Then we found Dr. Austin Richman at Veterinary Skin and Ear in Santa Monica, and everything changed.

From the moment we arrived, the facility, the team, and the level of expertise were on an entirely different level—warm, knowledgeable, detail-oriented, and clearly invested in helping even the most complicated cases. Dr. Richman reviewed Frank’s extensive history and was honest: one ear might have only a 30% chance of being saved because the damage was so advanced. But he said he wanted to try.

And thank goodness he did.

Dr. Richman performed a laser procedure to remove the extensive damaged tissue that had been blocking airflow and trapping infection for years—something no prior veterinarian had ever suggested. He also placed tubes in Frank’s ears (common in children yet somehow never mentioned to us before), which has been absolutely transformative.

The result: He saved BOTH ears!!!
No canal removal. No eardrum removal. No deafness. No extreme surgery. Just thoughtful, skilled, modern medicine.

Today, Frank can hear again. He’s happier, more energetic, more himself than he has been in years. We quite literally have our dog back.

I cannot overstate our gratitude to Dr. Richman and his incredible team. They gave our old boy a new chapter of life—one we weren’t sure he’d ever have.

If your dog is struggling with chronic skin or ear issues—even if you’ve been told there is no hope—go see Dr. Richman. He is simply exceptional.

Retaliatory, Price-Gouging Clinic That Abandoned Cancer Care & Withheld Records.

After years of bringing my Great Dane, Piper, to Veterinary Skin & Ear, I feel obligated to share my experience to protect other families navigating serious diagnoses. I paid this clinic more than $12,000 over several years. But when I finally asked for clarification on their sharply rising prices for an upcoming procedure, they abruptly cut off care.

Piper has lifelong skin cancer, requiring careful coordination between multiple veterinary specialists. I recently asked why a proposed cryotherapy treatment was priced at $1,600--a procedure my own dermatologist offers for under $200 using the same liquid nitrogen equipment. No explanation was provided. Instead, the clinic terminated Piper's care just days later, without any referral or continuity plan.

In my view, this was retaliation for asking a fair and appropriate question--and likely a violation of California veterinary law.
I requested Piper's full records and itemized invoices be sent to her care team. Instead, office manager Dawn McCoy delayed the records for weeks, then ignored my explicit instructions and failed to send them to the correct providers. When they finally arrived, the records were vague, incomplete, and included no breakdown of costs.

My follow-up questions were met with curt, unhelpful replies.
This clinic appears to operate on a model of price gouging and deflection, punishing clients who ask for transparency. The poor communication, record withholding, and lack of continuity reflect a deeper problem with how this clinic is run--and it starts with clinic owner Dr. Austin Richman and lead veterinarian Dr. Megan Boyd, whose decisions created the toxic and retaliatory culture I experienced.

I've filed formal complaints with the California Veterinary Medical Board and the Better Business Bureau, and I'm also considering legal action.

No animal with cancer should have their care disrupted like this. And no pet owner should be punished for asking a clinic to explain its billing.

----------------------------

*** Update: In response to the clinic's misleading reply to my review ***

This was never about a "lapse in communication." It was about an unethical decision to withhold my dog's medical records and abruptly terminate cancer care after I simply asked for a breakdown of charges and clinical notes.

Whether I contacted them in 2024 is irrelevant. Clients have a legal right to medical records at any time, and my request was reasonable and timely. The clinic is deflecting to avoid addressing their core behavior: refusing documentation, dodging responsibility, and retaliating when questioned.

Over the years, I paid this clinic more than $12,000 for my dog's care. This is how they treat longstanding, loyal clients.
